chunks: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a man said to him:

'The ones facing us are reporting that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Hates the house of meat.' So he said: 'They speak the truth, and it is not where you are going (with it). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Hates the house in which the meats of the people are eaten.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ حَيْثُ ذَهَبُوا: It is not where you are going (clarification of meaning)
key_terms.لُحُومُ النَّاسِ: Meats of the people (referring to their flesh/backbiting)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'house of meat' mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the literal interpretation of 'bayt al-lahm' by redefining it as a metaphor for a home where backbiting occurs, thereby elevating the merit of meat consumption to a spiritual plane. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, illustrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ta'wil* (interpretive depth) in everyday idioms, linking physical sustenance with ethical conduct. It serves as a reminder that the sanctity of a household is determined by the quality of its discourse rather than its material provisions.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>,

‘The ones facing us are reporting that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Hates the house of meat’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They speak the truth, and it is not where you are going (with it). Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Hates the house in which the meats of the people are eaten (backbiting takes place)’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Misma‘ abu Sayyar who has said the following: “Once, a man said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

‘People before us narrate that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, dislikes the house of meat.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘They have spoken the truth, but not as they think it is. It is in the sense that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, dislikes the house in which people eat other peoples’ meat (backbite them).”’
